text.title: This thread simply calls the 'receive' function of 'network_buffers_[0]' repeatedly, until stopped or when no more data is coming.

A smart buffer implemented on top of (deriving from) ring_buffer, adding extra functionality: the 'receive' function to read UDP packets from the socket, and interpretation of the CC header to look for missing packets, which are then automatically substituted with zero-fileld ones.
Creates an instance of class 'channel_data_extractor' and calls its 'run' member function which does the job.
Local variable of the thread, of type 'channel_data_extractor'

This class implements the algorithm to extract data from the UDP packets. Its 'run' member function continuously waits for new packets in the network buffer, and if there is a new packet, it extracts the data values of the individual channels, and pushes them into the per-channel data buffers.

These variables are vectors, or vector of vectors, of pointers pointing to the data buffers and other info (such as channel number, etc) asociated with the channels. These different vectors provide access to the channels in different ways, but the pointers point to the same objects.

The objects pointed to by the pointers in these vectors are 'ring_buffer's, which derive from the class 'channel_info' so that they do not only contain the sampled values from the channels, but also other channel-related info such as channel number, board number, etc.
